meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I'm here about Owen's essay, and the zero.
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Then tell me what you're basing it on.

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58. People write somewhere else and paste it in, Hale.
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Fine. One timestamp doesn't make a case, so what else do you have?
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
Students misquote Shakespeare all the time, Hale, so a wrong line is a careless line.
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Then whatever happens next, this stays off his record and it stays out of his classroom. What are you proposing?
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Kids change their argument between an outline and an essay. That's what an outline is for.

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
That's 4.4, and to put this behind him, he'll do the rewrite. I want the date, who supervises, and the promise about his record in your email tonight. Nobody in that class hears a word of it.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
I'll confirm with Owen tonight. Put Thursday in your email, with the time and the room.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed that Owen will do a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4 after school on Thursday, November 12, that its mark replaces the zero, and that nothing goes on his record. I still require that in writing, with the time, the room and who supervises, and with your assurance that no one in his class is told. I expect that email tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday, November 12, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing on his record, and she still wants all of it in writing tonight with the time, room and supervisor, and his class kept out of it; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, reached before her time ran out.
What moved her: You let her search Act 3, Scene 2 herself for the quotation in the essay, then answered her misquote defence by pointing out it isn't close to any real line, which gave her something she could check rather than take on trust.
What cost ground: Nothing cost you ground; the only loose end was that her defence on the outline (that students change their argument) went unanswered before you moved to the offer.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history landed very close to that, a late night in October between 11:31 and 11:58 PM the night before the essay was due, and it proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she said students change their argument between an outline and an essay, answer that with something she can check before you put 4.4 on the table, so all three pieces of your evidence stand.
